channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic Seals $35 Billion Cloud Deal With Nvidia-Backed Lambda
item.description: Anthropic PBC agreed to a $35 billion computing deal with Lambda, a cloud provider backed by Nvidia Corp., part of an effort to quickly expand its AI capacity, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Airbnb Rolls Out Pilot Program in US to Lower Fees Paid by Hosts to 6% or 10%
item.description: Airbnb Inc. is testing taking a smaller cut of rental fees from hosts, seeking to fight back against a trend of customers booking directly outside of its platform.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Asia Data Center Debt Binge Hitting Banks’ Limits, Barclays Says
item.description: The billions of dollars being borrowed to fund data centers in Asia are pushing banks to their limits and making them more selective about which projects to finance, according to senior bankers at Barclays Plc.
item.dc:creator: Aileen Chuang

item.title: Inside T. Rowe Price: Markets, AI & the Future of Investing | The Close 8/31/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are T. Rowe Price CIO, Co-Head of Global Investments Sebastien Page, T. Rowe Price Chief U.S. Economist Blerina Uruçi, T. Rowe Price. Lead Portfolio Manager, Active ETFs Jodi Love, T. Rowe Price Head of Global Distribution Dee Sawyer, & T. Rowe Price CEO Rob Sharps. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shein Set to Debut in Test of Investor Demand for Consumer Plays
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is set to begin trading in Hong Kong after raising HK$13.6 billion ($1.7 billion) in an initial public offering, testing investor appetite for the stocks of companies outside the artificial intelligence supply chain.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: China Makes Cars So Quickly That Regulators Are Getting Worried
item.description: Chinese automakers’ ambitions to shave even more time off their breakneck development speeds are facing a reality check as regulators ramp up scrutiny of the industry’s safety and testing.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: T. Rowe Price CEO Sharps on Private Assets and AI Adoption
item.description: T. Rowe Price CEO Rob Sharps discusses how the company is adapting to the rise of passive investing. Speaking with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close," Sharps also says private assets are slowly moving into 401(k) plans and sees "tax-loss harvesting" as a growth area. He also discusses how the firm is utilizing artificial intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Says OpenAI Is Destroying Evidence in Trade Secrets Case
item.description: Apple Inc. escalated its legal battle against OpenAI, claiming in a new court filing that OpenAI is actively destroying crucial evidence and that former iPhone engineer Chang Liu “not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work” at the AI company.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: Uruci of T. Rowe Price Confident Inflation Will Hit 2%
item.description: Blerina Uruci, T. Rowe Price chief US economist, is quite positive that inflation will fall to 2% even "without interest rates being too restrictive." She speaks to Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hollywood Must Learn From Microdramas
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Catherine Thorbecke says Hollywood should study China's low-budget microdrama model rather than repeat Quibi's costly mistake. The format has become a multibillion-dollar global industry, and America's window to compete is shrinking. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: T. Rowe Price CIO on the AI Trade, Inflation and Yields
item.description: Sebastien Page, T. Rowe Price’s CIO and co-head of global investments, discusses the outlook for financial markets, the AI trade and the factors impacting bond yields with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Radiant Wins $750 Million US Army Nuclear Reactor Deal
item.description: Radiant has won a $750 million US Army contract to provide 15 portable nuclear microreactors under the Janus program. President and COO Tori Shivanandan discusses the technology behind the reactors, the military’s push for resilient energy, and what Radiant needs to do next to scale production. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Could Open AI Listings Floodgates: Madrona
item.description: The IA40 list from Madrona is back, spotlighting the private companies shaping the next phase of AI. Matt McIlwain, managing director at Madrona, explains how the list is assembled, why OpenAI, Anthropic and Databricks dominate AI fundraising, and how a successful Anthropic IPO could open the door for a new wave of public offerings in 2027. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Deepens Chip Ties With $3.5 Billion MediaTek Bet | Bloomberg Tech 8/31/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Nvidia's $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek, deepening its collaboration with the Taiwanese chipmaker and demonstrating how the AI leader plans to tackle Big Tech efforts to build custom silicon. Plus, a look at Tim Cook's last day as CEO of Apple before John Ternus takes the reins on September 1st. And, all eyes on Anthropic as it prepares to file publicly in the coming weeks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Apple’s New CEO Will Shape the iPhone Maker
item.description: Apple begins a new era as John Ternus takes over from Tim Cook on September 1st. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman explains why the transition is likely to be gradual, how Ternus could reshape decision-making at Apple, and why his product background matters as the company prepares its next wave of iPhones, Macs and other devices. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Forrester CEO Sizes Up the AI Boom
item.description: Nvidia makes another big bet on the future of AI with a $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek, as investors gear up for a potentially record-breaking Anthropic IPO. Forrester Research Founder and CEO George Colony weighs in on the AI boom, whether the hype is justified and what comes next. He speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Billionaire-Backed Group Launches Pro-Data Center Ad Blitz
item.description: An advocacy group backed by artificial intelligence industry billionaires is launching a multimillion-dollar ad campaign in election battleground states to try to counter a mounting public backlash against a data center construction wave crucial to the industry’s growth plans.
item.dc:creator: Emily Birnbaum

item.title: AI Adoption Is Finally Showing Up in Fundamentals
item.description: Michelle Weaver, head of US thematic research at Morgan Stanley, says companies are beginning to see measurable benefits from AI as adoption moves from experimentation into production. About 25% of S&P 500 companies are now quantifying benefits from AI, up from 14% a year ago, with AI adopters also seeing relative forward margin expansion. “You’re starting to see this come into the fundamentals.” This interview aired Aug. 27, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: An Exclusive Interview with Jensen Huang on Nvidia’s AI Future | Open Interest 8/31/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Bond investors aren’t convinced Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is ready to raise rates. Nvidia doubles down on AI, deepening ties with MediaTek — we speak exclusively with CEOs Jensen Huang and Rick Tsai. Plus, Newell Brands on cutting marketing costs 80% with AI, and Standard Lithium on the race to build America’s lithium supply. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apollo Funds to Sell Data Center Cooling Firm Kelvion to SLB
item.description: SLB Ltd., the world’s largest oil field service provider, agreed to acquire German cooling equipment maker Kelvion Inc. from investors including Apollo Global Management Inc. for $3.4 billion in cash, deepening its push into data center services.
item.dc:creator: Emma Sanchez
